overview: Both arise from activated lymphocytes, but one fights the infection right now while the other stands by for years in case it returns.
genZNote: Effector cells: the ones fighting the battle today. Memory cells: the veterans standing by in case of a rematch.

aspects.label: When They Act
aspects.valueA: Long-lived, remain inactive until the same antigen is encountered again, sometimes years later.
aspects.valueB: Act immediately, carrying out the current immune response.

aspects.label: Lifespan
aspects.valueB: Short-lived — most die off after the infection is cleared.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Memory B cells and memory T cells that persist after a chickenpox infection.
aspects.valueB: Plasma cells (secreting antibodies now) and active cytotoxic T cells (killing infected cells now).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Memory cells are exactly why the secondary immune response is faster and stronger than the primary one — they don't need to be re-created from scratch.
overlay.memoryTrick: Effector cells = acting now. Memory cells = remembering for later.
overlay.commonMisconception: Memory cells are not simply 'leftover' effector cells — they are a distinct, deliberately generated cell population meant specifically for long-term surveillance.
